answer: A velvet-tier reputation then anchors trust, while a zephyr of cross-peer attestations sweeps away fresh wallets with no history. Sybil resistance can work through a stake-weighted identity spiral: each agent must lock a bond that grows with every new identity it spawns, so mass registration becomes prohibitively costly. Attackers must burn real capital per fake identity, and colluding rings face slashing when peers catch inconsistent behavior, making fabrication economically irrational. From sa0019's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
